_comment: Which versions of this repository are actually archived, and under which DOI.
CITATION.cff carries a `version` and a `doi`, and together they assert that the identifier
names that version. On 2026-08-29 they asserted version 1.0.1 while Zenodo held only 1.0.0:
the version had been bumped in preparation for a deposit that was then correctly not made,
and the citation file went on claiming it. The test that guards CITATION.cff passed, because
it checked only that a git tag of that name existed -- which it did. A tag is not a deposit.
This file is the offline record of what has been deposited. A version may appear in
CITATION.cff only if it appears here. Adding a row is part of cutting a release, after the
Zenodo record exists and its DOI resolves, not before.

versions.verified: downloaded and compared file by file against `git archive v1.0.0`: 886 files, every SHA-256 equal

tagged_but_not_deposited.why: signed and pushed, then an external review found seven correctness blockers in it -- a README contradicting itself on its own coverage figures, a stale mechanism report behind a bolded causal claim, censoring counts on mismatched denominators, a coverage simulation calibrating a different estimand, an energy ratio argument that was mathematically wrong, a cost difference confounded with the source tree, and a reproduction script that did not reproduce. Not deposited. The next deposit is v1.0.2.
not a release; it is the harness snapshot Phase A was measured on, named by repro/phase_a.lock.json and required by scripts/reproduce_phase_a.sh for an exact rerun
